AccountResponse.description:
The caller's own account.

Overlaps ``CurrentUserResponse`` from ``/auth/me`` and is deliberately a
separate model. ``/auth/me`` answers "who am I, and what CSRF token should
I send" — it is part of the authentication handshake and carries the CSRF
token. This answers "what does my account look like", carries no token,
and is free to grow fields that the authentication path should not.

display_name.description: Null when the account has no separate label; render the username.
display_name.title: Display Name

last_login_at.description: ISO-8601, or null if this account has never signed in. On the caller's own account this is the *previous* sign-in's timestamp only until the current one records it, which happens at login — so it reflects the current session.
last_login_at.title: Last Login At

AccountResponse.title: AccountResponse

AgentReleasesResponse.description: What this controller knows about installable agents.

available.description: Whether a verified download is on offer. False means no release manifest is configured, which is the state of any build made before the first release was published — the interface then shows the build-from-source path rather than a download command whose URL would not resolve.
available.title: Available

minimum_supported_version.description: The oldest agent version this controller is known to work with. Advisory: the protocol version is what a connection negotiates, and nothing is refused on the strength of this field.
minimum_supported_version.title: Minimum Supported Version

platforms.description: The architectures on offer, in the order to present them.

supported_protocol_versions.description: Every protocol version this controller will accept on a connection.

unavailable_reason.description: Why there is nothing to download. Null when `available`.
unavailable_reason.title: Unavailable Reason

api_version.description: API major version served under this prefix.
api_version.title: Api Version

An account referenced by an event.

``username`` is null when the account no longer exists. The id is always
present, because that is what the trail actually recorded — see
:mod:`hcc.services.audit` on why names are joined rather than
snapshotted.

username.title: Username

action.description: A dotted action identifier such as `user.role_changed`. A string rather than a closed enum, because the vocabulary grows with every milestone that records something new (ADR-038) — a client must render an unrecognised value rather than failing on it.
action.title: Action

actor.description: Who performed it, or null for an operation with no authenticated actor.

Desired versus applied.

The distinction §23 insists on: a configuration the controller has saved is
not thereby active. ``status`` describes the gap.

desired_version.description: Newest revision the controller has generated.
desired_version.title: Desired Version

batch_size.title: Batch Size

canary_host_ids.title: Canary Host Ids

health_check_seconds.title: Health Check Seconds

CurrentUserResponse.description:
The authenticated identity.

Carries no password material and no session token. ``csrf_token`` is
included because the client needs it to make state-changing requests, and
it is useless without the session cookie.

display_name.description: Human-readable label, or null when the account has none. Added in milestone 1.7 so the console can greet the user by the name an administrator gave them rather than by their login name. Null means 'no separate label' — render the username.

username.description: Display form, as the user entered it.
username.title: Username

CurrentUserResponse.title: CurrentUserResponse

EffectiveModuleResponse.description:
One module's effective configuration on one host, with its provenance.

Both stored layers are reported alongside the resolved value, because
"inherited from the global default of 10 s" and "overridden on this host to
10 s" are identical in the value and are different facts.

host_override.description: The host's own override, or null when this host has none at all.

EffectiveModuleResponse.title: EffectiveModuleResponse

EnrollRequest.description:
What an agent tells the controller about itself while enrolling.

Every field is optional and advisory. There is deliberately no
``host_id``, no ``hostname`` and no ``host_name``: the host is decided by
the enrollment credential, and a field naming a host would be a field an
agent could use to claim a different one.

agent_version.description: The agent's own version string. Advisory, never trusted.
agent_version.title: Agent Version

EnrollRequest.title: EnrollRequest

EnrollResponse.description:
The agent's new identity.

``credential`` is the long-lived agent credential and this is the only
time it crosses the network in this direction. The agent writes it to a
file only it can read; the controller keeps only its digest.

credential.description: The long-lived agent credential, in plaintext. Store it with restrictive permissions; it is not retrievable again.
credential.title: Credential

heartbeat_interval_seconds.description: How often the controller expects a heartbeat once connected.
heartbeat_interval_seconds.title: Heartbeat Interval Seconds

host_id.description: The host this agent is now the agent for.
host_id.title: Host Id

host_name.description: Display name, so the agent's log and `status` output name the host an operator recognises rather than a UUID.
host_name.title: Host Name

protocol_version.description: The protocol version this controller speaks.
protocol_version.title: Protocol Version

superseded_previous.description: Whether this enrollment revoked a credential the host already had. True means another agent has just been cut off — reported so the agent's own log says it took over rather than joined.
superseded_previous.title: Superseded Previous

EnrollResponse.title: EnrollResponse

EnrollmentResponse.description:
A freshly issued enrollment credential.

**The only response in the API that contains a secret.** The credential is
not stored — only its digest is — so this body cannot be reproduced by any
later request, including a retry of this one. The interface has to show it
once and say so.

credential.description: The one-time enrollment credential, in plaintext. Shown once and never retrievable again. Single use, scoped to this host, and revocable until used.
credential.title: Credential

expires_in_seconds.description: Convenience for a countdown, computed server-side so the display does not depend on the browser's clock being right.
expires_in_seconds.title: Expires In Seconds

superseded.description: How many previously-pending credentials this issuance revoked. Non-zero means an earlier credential for this host has just stopped working, which an administrator needs to be told rather than discover by watching an agent fail.
superseded.title: Superseded

EnrollmentResponse.title: EnrollmentResponse

ErrorDetail.description: The ``error`` member of an error response.

details.description: Optional structured context, e.g. field validation errors.
details.title: Details

request_id.description: Correlates this response with server-side logs.
request_id.title: Request Id

ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail

ErrorResponse.description: The complete body of any non-2xx API response.
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

blocked.description: A newer release exists and something stops it. Still an update.
blocked.title: Blocked

metadata_available.description: Whether release metadata is configured. Not the same as 'no updates'.
metadata_available.title: Metadata Available

metadata_signature.description: valid | absent | untrusted_key | invalid | malformed | unsupported_algorithm. An automatic update needs 'valid'.
metadata_signature.title: Metadata Signature

needs_attention.description: Unsupported or unreadable versions — hosts somebody has to look at.
needs_attention.title: Needs Attention

version_distribution.description: Newest first. Unparseable versions last and visible rather than hidden.
version_distribution.title: Version Distribution

GlobalDefaultResponse.description: A global default, keyed by module.
GlobalDefaultResponse.title: GlobalDefaultResponse

GlobalDefaultSavedResponse.description: What a global-default save did, including how far it reached.

hosts_changed.description: How many hosts' effective configuration this changed. Not every host: one that overrides this module is unaffected, and saying so lets the interface report '12 of 30 changed' rather than implying the whole fleet moved.
hosts_changed.title: Hosts Changed

GlobalDefaultSavedResponse.title: GlobalDefaultSavedResponse

GlobalDefaultsResponse.description:
Every global default.

Modules with nothing configured are present with both fields null, so the
interface renders the full catalogue from one response and "nothing has
been said about this module" is a value rather than a missing key.
GlobalDefaultsResponse.title: GlobalDefaultsResponse

HostConnectivity.description:
Whether an agent is attached *right now*.

Three states, not two, and the third is the one that makes this honest.
HostConnectivity.title: HostConnectivity

HostCreateRequest.description:
Register a host.

``extra="forbid"``: a request naming a field this model does not declare
is rejected. That is the mass-assignment guard at the boundary — a
forwarded ``lifecycle``, ``connection_epoch`` or ``id`` fails validation
rather than being silently dropped, and a client that believed it set one
finds out.

description.description: Optional note, up to 512 characters after normalization. Blank or whitespace-only is stored as null.
description.title: Description

environment.description: Optional grouping label, up to 32 characters. For the operator's own use; nothing resolves configuration against it.
environment.title: Environment

name.description: 1 to 64 characters after normalization. Case-insensitively unique. Interior spaces are allowed; runs of whitespace are collapsed.
name.title: Name

HostCreateRequest.title: HostCreateRequest

allow_reenrollment.description: Required to issue a credential for a host that already has an enrolled agent. Consuming the new credential revokes the existing one and disconnects that agent, so the confirmation is the difference between a deliberate re-enrollment and a misclick that takes a working host offline.
allow_reenrollment.title: Allow Reenrollment

HostLifecycle.description:
How far through enrollment a host record has got.

A small closed set stored as a constrained ``varchar`` rather than a native
PostgreSQL enum. The reasoning is ADR-038's, applied here: this is not an
authorization surface, so a future member should not require
``ALTER TYPE`` — but it *is* closed today, so a CHECK does the enforcing.
HostLifecycle.title: HostLifecycle

HostListResponse.description: A page of hosts, and what a pager needs.

total.description: Hosts matching the name, lifecycle and status filters, ignoring pagination. The `connectivity` filter is applied to the page after it is fetched, so when one is supplied this total counts the hosts the other filters matched and `items` may be shorter than `limit`. Deliberate — see hcc/services/hosts.py.
total.title: Total

HostListResponse.title: HostListResponse

problems.description: Adjustments the controller made on the operator's behalf — an interval raised to a module's current floor, configuration for a module this release no longer has. Not errors: the configuration is valid and in use. Shown so a setting that does something other than what it says cannot do so silently.
problems.title: Problems

HostResponse.description:
One host, as the interface sees it.

An allow-list. See the module docstring for what is deliberately absent
and why "absent" is a stronger statement than "excluded".

agent_started_at.description: When the connected agent process started, as it reports. Advisory.
agent_started_at.title: Agent Started At

agent_version.description: As the agent reports it. Advisory and untrusted — it comes from a possibly-compromised host and is never used for a decision.
agent_version.title: Agent Version

connectivity.description: Derived from whether a connection is recorded and how recent the last heartbeat is — never read from a stored flag. 'stale' means a connection is recorded but the heartbeats stopped, which is the honest answer when the controller cannot tell whether the agent died or the network did.

credential_issued_at.description: When the live agent credential was issued, or null when there is none. Distinguishes 'never enrolled' from 'credential revoked' without disclosing anything about the credential.
credential_issued_at.title: Credential Issued At

description.description: Operator's note, or null when there is none. Null means 'no note', not 'unknown'.
description.title: Description

environment.description: Free-text grouping label for the operator's own use, or null.
environment.title: Environment

has_pending_enrollment.description: Whether an unused, unexpired enrollment credential exists. A boolean and nothing more: the credential itself is unrecoverable once issued.
has_pending_enrollment.title: Has Pending Enrollment

is_enabled.description: Whether the operator currently wants this host connected. A disabled host keeps its enrollment and its history; its agent is refused at the door.
is_enabled.title: Is Enabled

last_heartbeat_at.description: ISO-8601, or null when no agent has ever reported. Null must not be rendered as a date.
last_heartbeat_at.title: Last Heartbeat At

lifecycle.description: How far through enrollment this host is. Independent of connectivity.

name.description: Display form of the name, as it was entered.
name.title: Name

protocol_version.description: Protocol major version negotiated on the last connection, or null.
protocol_version.title: Protocol Version

HostResponse.title: HostResponse

revision_created.description: False when the save changed nothing the agent would notice — a setting written back identical to what it already was. The configuration is correct either way; this says whether a new revision was minted.
revision_created.title: Revision Created

revision_version.description: The revision this produced, or the existing one.
revision_version.title: Revision Version

HostUpdateRequest.description:
Change a host's labels.

Every field is optional, and "absent" is distinguished from "null":
omitting ``description`` leaves it alone, sending ``null`` clears it.
Pydantic cannot express that with a plain default, so
:meth:`to_service_update` consults ``model_fields_set`` — the set of keys
the client actually sent.

Labels only. ``lifecycle``, ``is_enabled`` and every connectivity column
are deliberately absent: enrollment state is changed by enrolling or
revoking, administrative state by the enable and disable endpoints, and
connectivity by an agent connecting. A field here that could set any of
them would let an administrator type a host into a state the system had
not reached.

description.description: Send a string to set it, null to clear it, or omit the key.
description.title: Description

environment.description: Send a string to set it, null to clear it, or omit the key.
environment.title: Environment

name.description: Omit to leave unchanged. Null is treated as omitted.
name.title: Name

HostUpdateRequest.title: HostUpdateRequest

HostUpdateStatusResponse.description: Everything the interface shows for one host.

automatic.description: Whether this host installs anything by itself.
automatic.title: Automatic

HostUpdateStatusResponse.title: HostUpdateStatusResponse

LatestResponse.description:
A host's current values.

Empty when the host has produced nothing recent — not a list of zeroes.
The interface renders "no data", which is the honest answer and is
distinguishable from a measurement of zero.

freshness_seconds.description: How recent a sample had to be to appear here. Reported so the interface can say 'no data in the last 5 minutes' rather than 'no data', which are different claims.
freshness_seconds.title: Freshness Seconds

LatestResponse.title: LatestResponse

LatestValueResponse.description: The most recent value of one series.
LatestValueResponse.title: LatestValueResponse

LivenessResponse.description: Deliberately minimal: this endpoint is public.
LivenessResponse.title: LivenessResponse

LoginPayload.description:
Login request body.

Bounded by Pydantic so oversized input is refused before any of our code
sees it. ``model_config`` forbids extra fields: a typo'd key should be an
error, not something silently dropped.
LoginPayload.title: LoginPayload

MaintenanceWindowRequest.description: When this host may be interrupted.

end.description: Local wall-clock HH:MM. Equal to start means all day.
end.title: End

timezone.description: IANA zone name, e.g. Europe/Berlin. Required: 02:00 means 02:00 somewhere.
timezone.title: Timezone

weekdays.description: 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday. Empty means every day.
weekdays.title: Weekdays

MaintenanceWindowRequest.title: MaintenanceWindowRequest

MaintenanceWindowResponse.description: When a host is willing to be interrupted.

description.description: One line for display, naming the zone.
description.title: Description

end.description: Local wall-clock HH:MM. Equal to start means all day.
end.title: End

timezone.description: IANA zone name. Always present, never implied.
timezone.title: Timezone

weekdays.description: 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday. Empty means every day.
weekdays.title: Weekdays

MaintenanceWindowResponse.title: MaintenanceWindowResponse

MetricResponse.description:
One series a module produces, declared before any sample arrives.

The interface needs units and labels up front, so that an enabled module
with no data yet renders as "no data" rather than as nothing at all.

kind.description: gauge | counter. A counter is never averaged.
kind.title: Kind

label_keys.description: Dimensions this metric is broken down by — 'core' for per-core CPU, 'window' for the three load averages. Empty means one series per host.
label_keys.title: Label Keys

MetricResponse.title: MetricResponse

MetricsStatusResponse.description:
Whether anything is actually arriving.

The answer to the question an operator asks before looking at a chart, and
the one a chart cannot answer. An empty chart has four possible causes and
only one of them is visible from the data:

1. **Nothing has been collected** — this endpoint.
2. **Collection is switched off** — the monitoring endpoint.
3. **The agent is offline** — the host endpoint.
4. **Collection is on, the agent is connected, and the collector is
   failing every interval** — this endpoint too, through
   :class:`ModuleStatusResponse`'s error fields.

The fourth was unreported until Phase M. The agent had always sent the
reason; the controller parsed it and threw it away.

last_sample_at.description: The newest sample across every series, or null if there are none.
last_sample_at.title: Last Sample At

modules.description: Every module in the registry, including those that have produced nothing — so the interface can distinguish 'this module has no data' from 'this module does not exist'.
modules.title: Modules

sample_count.description: Raw samples stored for this host, across every series and partition.
sample_count.title: Sample Count

MetricsStatusResponse.title: MetricsStatusResponse

ModuleCatalogueResponse.description: Everything that can be configured, and the limits that apply to all of it.

document_version.description: Version of the configuration document shape.
document_version.title: Document Version

min_interval_seconds.description: Global interval floor, across every module.
min_interval_seconds.title: Min Interval Seconds

registry_version.description: Version of the catalogue as a whole. Distinct from the protocol version: adding a module must not force a fleet upgrade.
registry_version.title: Registry Version

ModuleCatalogueResponse.title: ModuleCatalogueResponse

ModuleResponse.description: A module as the interface needs to present it.

default_interval_seconds.description: The interval offered when an operator enables this module. NOT a default to run: every module ships disabled.
default_interval_seconds.title: Default Interval Seconds

min_interval_seconds.description: The floor. Collecting faster is refused.
min_interval_seconds.title: Min Interval Seconds

schedule_kinds.description: Which scheduling kinds this module accepts. Enforced on save.
schedule_kinds.title: Schedule Kinds

ModuleResponse.title: ModuleResponse

ModuleSettingRequest.description:
A change to one module at one layer.

``model_fields_set`` distinguishes absent from null, which is the whole
reason this is not two optional fields with ``None`` defaults — see the
module docstring.

enabled.description: True to collect, false not to, null to inherit the layer above. Omit the field entirely to leave it unchanged.
enabled.title: Enabled

schedule.description: A schedule document — {'kind': 'interval', 'interval_seconds': N} or a calendar schedule — or null to inherit. Omit to leave unchanged. Validated against the module's permitted kinds and its interval floor; every problem is returned at once.
schedule.title: Schedule

ModuleSettingRequest.title: ModuleSettingRequest

ModuleStatusResponse.description:
What one module is doing on one host.

The last five fields answer a question the first four could not: **is the
collector failing?** A module with ``series_count`` of zero and a
``last_sample_at`` of null could be one nobody enabled, one enabled a
second ago, or one that has raised the same error every interval for a
week. Those need different actions and used to look identical.

consecutive_failures.description: Failures since the last success. Zero both for a module that is working and for one that has never reported; `last_reported_at` tells those apart.
consecutive_failures.title: Consecutive Failures

last_error.description: Why the last collection produced nothing, usually in the agent's own words. Kept after a later success — only the failure count resets — so a module that fails and recovers every few minutes is visible rather than self-erasing. Untrusted text from the host: display it, do not interpret it.
last_error.title: Last Error

last_error_at.description: When the last failure arrived, or null if none ever has.
last_error_at.title: Last Error At

last_reported_at.description: When the controller last heard anything about this module — a successful collection or a failed one. Null means this host has never reported it, which is not the same as healthy.
last_reported_at.title: Last Reported At

last_sample_at.description: When this module last produced a sample, on the *agent's* clock, or null if it never has.
last_sample_at.title: Last Sample At

last_success_at.description: When a collection last arrived without an error. A collection that ran and produced no samples counts: a rate collector's first interval legitimately produces nothing.
last_success_at.title: Last Success At

series_count.description: How many series this module has produced.
series_count.title: Series Count

ModuleStatusResponse.title: ModuleStatusResponse

PasswordChangeRequest.description:
Change the caller's own password.

Confirmation of the new password is deliberately **not** a field. It is a
client-side guard against a typo in a masked input, and the server has
nothing to compare it against that the client does not already have — so
sending it would mean transmitting the new password twice for no gain. The
interface enforces the match before submitting.

current_password.description: Proof that the caller is the account's owner, not merely its session.
current_password.title: Current Password

PasswordChangeRequest.title: PasswordChangeRequest

PasswordChangeResponse.description:
What the password change did.

No password material, and no token: the replacement session travels in
``Set-Cookie``, where the client cannot read it (``HttpOnly``) and does not
need to.

other_sessions_revoked.description: How many *other* sessions were ended. The current one was replaced rather than counted here, so zero means this was the only place the account was signed in.
other_sessions_revoked.title: Other Sessions Revoked

session_expires_at.description: ISO-8601 expiry of the replacement session.
session_expires_at.title: Session Expires At

PasswordChangeResponse.title: PasswordChangeResponse

PlatformArtifactResponse.description: One architecture's download, with the digest that pins it.

sha256.description: The archive's SHA-256. Rendered into the install command so that `sha256sum -c -` fails before the `tar` if the bytes are not the bytes this controller expects.
sha256.title: Sha256

tier.description: `supported` — built, executed and covered by the installation matrix. `best-effort` — built and executed under emulation only, with no hardware behind the claim.
tier.title: Tier

PlatformArtifactResponse.title: PlatformArtifactResponse

RangePointResponse.description:
One point of a historical series.

``minimum`` and ``maximum`` are present only for a rolled-up tier. They
are not decoration: a downsampled series drawn as a single line of
averages loses the spikes the operator enabled fast sampling to catch, so
the interface draws a min-max band and needs the bounds to do it.

sample_count.description: How many raw samples this bucket aggregates. Present only for a rolled-up tier, and what makes a partially-filled bucket visible rather than indistinguishable from a full one.
sample_count.title: Sample Count

RangePointResponse.title: RangePointResponse

RangeResponse.description: A historical series over a time range.

points.description: Ordered by time, with **no points for empty buckets**. A gap is a gap: nothing here is interpolated, so the interface draws a break rather than a line through a period when nothing was collected.
points.title: Points

resolution.description: raw | 5m | 1h — which tier answered. Reported because 'this is hourly data' is information needed to interpret a flat-looking graph.
resolution.title: Resolution

truncated.description: Whether the point budget cut the series short. Only reachable when the caller named a resolution the range does not suit; the automatic choice always fits.
truncated.title: Truncated

RangeResponse.title: RangeResponse

ReadinessResponse.description:
Aggregate only: this endpoint is public.

Which dependency failed, and why, is logged server-side rather than
returned — see the module docstring.
ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse

ResolvedEnabledResponse.description: Whether a module collects on this host, and which layer decided.

source.description: default | global | host. 'default' means nothing is configured, which resolves to off. The source is why an interface can answer 'why is this host collecting every five seconds?'.
source.title: Source

ResolvedEnabledResponse.title: ResolvedEnabledResponse

ResolvedScheduleResponse.description: The schedule a module runs on, and which layer decided.

next_runs.description: For a calendar schedule, the next few executions as ISO-8601 instants. Null for an interval schedule, where the next run is arithmetic rather than a calculation worth previewing.
next_runs.title: Next Runs

value.description: The fully resolved schedule, exactly as the agent receives it. Every value is concrete — `jitter_seconds` is resolved, never omitted — because the agent merges nothing.
value.title: Value

ResolvedScheduleResponse.title: ResolvedScheduleResponse

RevisionListResponse.description: A page of a host's configuration history, newest first.
RevisionListResponse.title: RevisionListResponse

RevisionResponse.description:
One historical configuration, without its document.

The document is several kilobytes and is not included in a list: a page of
twenty would be most of a megabyte, and the interface needs the versions
and their outcomes rather than the bytes.
RevisionResponse.title: RevisionResponse

revoked.description: How many credentials were revoked. Zero means there were none to revoke — the request succeeded and changed nothing.
revoked.title: Revoked

RolloutControlRequest.description: Pausing, resuming or cancelling, with a reason for the audit trail.

override_failures.description: On resume: go on despite the failures that paused it. Without this, a rollout stopped by the failure gate pauses again on the next pass — which is correct and would otherwise look like a bug.
override_failures.title: Override Failures

RolloutControlRequest.title: RolloutControlRequest

RolloutMemberResponse.description: One host's place in a rollout, and where it has got to.

batch.description: 0 is the canary; 1 and up are the batches, in order.
batch.title: Batch

healthy.description: Whether the post-install health check has passed. False while a host is still settling, and false for one that installed and then went away — which is the distinction the next batch waits on.
healthy.title: Healthy

RolloutMemberResponse.title: RolloutMemberResponse

RolloutResponse.description: A rollout and its current progress.

info.description:
Control plane API for Homelab Control Center — a self-hosted platform for
monitoring and managing Linux hosts, Docker containers and network devices.

This is pre-release software. The surface implemented today is identity and
access (authentication, sessions, users, audit), the host registry and its
enrolment flow, monitoring configuration, and metric ingestion and query.

Docker, logs, alerting, network checks and remote management are documented
in the repository but **not implemented**, and have no endpoints here.
info.title: Homelab Control Center

get.description:
Return the caller's account details.

Reads from the user already loaded with the session, so this costs no
additional query.

post.description:
Replace the caller's password, ending every session and issuing a new one.

Requires the current password even though the caller already holds a valid
session. A session proves possession of a cookie; changing a credential
should require possession of the credential, so that a stolen session
cannot be used to lock the real owner out of their own account.

A wrong current password is **422, never 401**. The client treats 401 as
"your session has ended" and signs the user out, so returning it here
would eject someone for a typo — see
:class:`~hcc.services.account.InvalidCurrentPasswordError`.

422.description: The current password did not verify, or the new one violates the policy. The two are distinguished by `error.code`.

429.description: Too many attempts for this account. Carries Retry-After.

get.description:
List every session that would currently authenticate the caller.

Only live ones. Expired and revoked rows are kept in the table so that
"when did this session end" stays answerable, but they are not what
"where am I signed in" means and listing them would bury the answer.

post.description:
End every session except this one.

Declared before the ``{session_id}`` route below so that ``revoke-others``
is not captured as a session id. FastAPI matches in declaration order, and
the parameter is typed as a UUID so the literal would in fact fall through
with a 422 rather than being mistaken for one — but relying on a
validation failure for correct routing is the kind of thing that breaks
the day someone widens the type.
post.summary: Sign out of every other session

post.description:
End one session.

Revoking the current session is allowed — that is a sign-out, and the
client learns on its next request, which answers 401. Refusing it would
mean one row in the list behaved differently from the others for no reason
the user could see.

A session id belonging to another account returns 404, identically to one
that does not exist, so this cannot be used to discover whose sessions are
live.

404.description: No live session of the caller's has that id.

post.summary: Revoke one of the caller's sessions

get.description:
Return the install manifest, or say why there is none.

**200 in both cases.** "No release has been published" is a fact about
this deployment, not an error in the request — a 404 would make the
interface treat a perfectly healthy controller as broken, and a 503 would
say the controller is unavailable when it is the download that is.
get.summary: The agent releases this controller can vouch for

post.description:
Claim a host, once, with the credential an administrator issued.

The enrollment credential is spent by this call and cannot be used again —
including by a retry of this request. An agent whose network dropped
*after* the controller committed but before the response arrived has lost
its credential and must be issued another; that is the cost of single use,
and the alternative — a credential usable twice — is a credential that can
be replayed by whoever read it over somebody's shoulder.

**200, not 201.** Nothing addressable was created: the host already
existed, and what came back is a credential rather than a resource with a
URL. A 201 would imply a ``Location``, and there is none — there is no
endpoint that returns this credential again.

Every refusal is a 401 with one message. Expired, already used, revoked and
never-existed are indistinguishable to the caller on purpose; the audit
trail records which it was, because an administrator can act on that and an
attacker holding a stolen credential cannot.

401.description: No credential presented, or it is not usable.

post.summary: Exchange a one-time enrollment credential for an agent credential

get.description:
Return the action identifiers this server can record.

Served so the interface can offer a filter without hard-coding a list
that drifts from the server's. It describes what this build *writes*, not
what the table *contains* — a stored event from an older or newer version
may carry an action absent from here, which is exactly why the filter
accepts any string and the renderer tolerates an unknown one.

A constant, so there is no query and nothing to paginate.

post.description:
Verify credentials and issue a session.

Session fixation is impossible by construction: the token is generated
server-side from a CSPRNG and nothing the client sends influences it. Any
session already presented is revoked before the new one is issued, so a
token planted in the browser before login cannot survive it.

401.description: Invalid credentials. Identical for every cause.

post.description:
Revoke the current session server-side and clear its cookies.

Requires a valid session and a valid CSRF token: without the CSRF check, a
cross-site request could log a user out, which is a minor but real
nuisance attack.

Revocation is server-side and immediate. The cookie clearing is a
courtesy — the session is dead whether or not the client complies.

get.description:
Return the current user, and the CSRF token for subsequent requests.

This is how a client that has a session cookie but no in-memory state —
after a page reload, say — recovers both its identity and its CSRF token.

Report, never act. See the note above this handler.

Available to every authenticated role: "is the controller current" is a
question anybody looking after this installation may ask, and the answer
holds no secret — a schema revision and two counts.

get.description:
Return a page of hosts.

Available to every authenticated role, because a Viewer who cannot see the
fleet cannot use a monitoring product. Nothing in the response is
privileged: it is the same host metadata the dashboard renders, with no
credential material and no digests.

``limit`` is bounded by the query validation *and* clamped again in the
service. Two layers on purpose: this is the bound that stops an
authenticated caller asking the server to materialise every host, and a
bound enforced in only one place is one a future caller can route around.

post.description:
Register a host and return it.

The new host is ``registered``, enabled, and has **no** enrollment
credential. Registering a record and authorising an agent to claim it are
two decisions, and bundling them would mean every mistyped host also
minted a live secret with a fifteen-minute life.

409.description: The host name is already in use.

422.description: The name, description or environment is invalid.

get.description:
Return one host.

``host_id`` is typed as a UUID, so a malformed id is a 422 from the
framework and never reaches a query.

patch.description:
Change a host's labels.

Partial by design: a request naming only ``description`` leaves the name
alone. An empty body is accepted and changes nothing, which is the honest
answer — refusing it would mean the client had to decide whether its own
diff was empty, and a no-op is not an error.

Renaming is permitted, and the agent's access is unaffected: a credential
is bound to the host's id, not to its name. A host name is a label the
operator reads, which is why it is mutable where a username is not
(ADR-041).

409.description: The new name is already in use.

patch.summary: Change a host's name, description or environment

post.description:
Withdraw trust from this host's agent.

The agent is cut off at its next authentication attempt, which for a
connected agent is immediately: the controller closes a connection whose
credential has stopped being live.

The host moves to ``revoked``, which is deliberately not ``registered``.
The record has been used, and re-enrolling a host that once had an agent is
a different decision from enrolling one for the first time — collapsing the
two would hide the fact that a credential was ever issued.

A host with no live credential is a 409, not a success. "Revoked" and
"there was nothing to revoke" are different answers, and an interface that
conflated them would tell an operator their host is secured when nothing
happened.

409.description: The host has no active agent credential.

post.description:
Refuse this host's agent at the door, keeping its enrollment.

Takes effect immediately: a connected agent's connection is closed, and
further authentication attempts are refused while the host is disabled.

Distinct from revoking the credential. Disabling is "not right now" and is
undone by enabling; revoking is "that secret is no longer trusted" and is
undone only by re-enrolling the agent. An interface that offered one
control for both would force the operator to choose a consequence they had
not been told about.

Idempotent — disabling an already-disabled host succeeds and records
nothing.

Allow this host's agent to connect again.

Does not reconnect anything by itself, and must not: the controller never
dials out to a host (ADR-018). The agent is retrying on its own backoff
schedule and will succeed on its next attempt.

Mint the credential an agent uses to claim this host, once.

**The returned credential is the only copy.** Only its SHA-256 digest is
stored (ADR-042), so no later request can produce it — there is no "show
again", and the interface says so instead of offering a control that would
have to lie.

Issuing revokes any still-pending credential for this host, so the one on
screen is the only one that works. ``superseded`` reports how many stopped
working, because an administrator who issued a credential ten minutes ago
needs to know the old one is dead rather than find out when an agent fails.

A host that already has a live agent credential is refused unless
``allow_reenrollment`` is true: consuming this credential revokes that one
and disconnects the running agent, which is a consequence the caller has to
accept explicitly.

Issuing for a **disabled** host is permitted. Enrollment and connection are
separate steps, and preparing a host before enabling it is a reasonable
order of operations — the agent will enroll and then be refused at the door
until the host is enabled, which the host detail view states.

409.description: The host already has an enrolled agent.

post.description:
Kill an enrollment credential that has not been used yet.

The "I pasted that into the wrong window" action. Takes effect
immediately, and cannot be undone — issue a new credential instead.

Returns the count rather than asserting success, so "there was nothing
pending" is distinguishable from "one was revoked". An unknown id is a 404
rather than a cheerful zero, because a revocation that reports success
without having revoked anything is the one thing this must not do.
post.summary: Revoke a host's pending enrollment credentials

get.description:
The newest value of each series, if it is recent enough to be current.

The freshness window is the whole design of this endpoint. Returning a
host's newest sample regardless of age would let the interface present a
three-day-old CPU reading as the current one, and nothing in the response
would say otherwise. An absent series renders as "no data", which is
honest and distinguishable from a measurement of zero.

get.description:
The question a chart cannot answer.

An empty chart could mean "nothing collected", "collection is off", "the
agent is offline" or "the collector is failing", and only the first is
visible from the data. This endpoint answers the first and the fourth; the
monitoring endpoint answers the second and the host endpoint the third.

Every module in the registry appears, including those that have produced
nothing, so the interface can tell "this module has no data" from "this
module does not exist on this controller".
get.summary: Whether metrics are actually arriving for a host

get.description:
Every module's resolved settings for one host, with provenance.

Reports the resolved value *and* both stored layers, because the question
an operator asks is not "what is the interval" but "why is it that".

delete.description:
Remove this host's override, so it inherits again.

A ``DELETE`` rather than a ``PUT`` of all-nulls: "stop overriding this
module entirely" is one intention and should be one request. Idempotent —
resetting a module that was already inherited succeeds, and is recorded,
because "did anyone try to change this?" is a question the audit trail
should be able to answer.

**200 with a body**, not 204. The caller needs the resulting revision and
sync status in order to show what the reset actually did, and a 204 would
make that a second request against state that may already have moved.

404.description: No such host, or no such module.

delete.summary: Make a host inherit the global default for one module

put.description:
Make this host differ from the global default for one module.

The response reports ``revision_created`` and the sync status rather than
just success, because §23 draws a line this endpoint sits exactly on: a
configuration the controller has saved is **not** thereby active. The
agent has to receive it, validate it and apply it, and until it does the
status is ``pending``.

404.description: No such host, or no such module.

422.description: The schedule was refused; every problem is listed.

put.summary: Set or clear one module's override on one host

get.description:
Every configuration this host has been given, newest first.

Offset pagination, unlike the audit log's keyset. The justification is the
scale: a host accumulates a revision per configuration change, which is
operator-paced rather than event-paced, so the deep-offset degradation
keyset pagination exists to avoid is not reachable here. The audit log,
which grows per request, genuinely needs keyset.

The documents themselves are not included — see
:class:`RevisionResponse`.

put.description:
Change what this host may do by itself. Audited.

The audit row records whether the result is automatic, because the moment
a host starts updating itself is the fact somebody will want to find.

post.summary: Start an update on one host

get.description:
Return metadata about the running control plane.

Authenticated, not public. The release version and environment name are of
no use to a legitimate anonymous caller and of obvious use to someone
matching the deployment against known vulnerabilities.

What every host does unless it overrides it.

Every module in the catalogue appears, including those with nothing
configured — both fields null — so the interface renders the whole list
from one response and does not have to treat a missing key as a value.

put.description:
Change the fleet-wide default for one module.

**200, not 201.** Nothing addressable is created: the resource is the
module's default, which exists conceptually whether or not a row backs it,
and this endpoint is idempotent — sending the same body twice leaves the
same state and mints no second revision.

Regenerates the affected hosts' configuration revisions in the same
transaction, so a host's desired configuration cannot lag the default it
is supposed to inherit. Bounded: past
:data:`hcc.services.monitoring.MAX_EAGER_REGENERATION` hosts the remainder
pick the change up on their next connection, which regenerates anyway.

422.description: The schedule was refused; every problem is listed.

put.summary: Set or clear a global module default

get.description:
The closed catalogue, with the limits that bound every schedule.

Static for a given release — it is the registry, which is code — so it
takes no database session and does no query. Served from an authenticated
route rather than a public one anyway: the module list describes what this
deployment is capable of collecting, which is of no use to an anonymous
caller and of some use to someone profiling the deployment.
get.summary: Every monitoring module this controller supports

get.description:
Report whether an initial administrator exists.

Reads the installation row rather than counting users, matching the
invariant bootstrap itself enforces (ADR-033): an installation stays
initialized even if every account is later removed, so this must not start
reporting "setup required" when the last user is deleted.

post.description:
Fail updates whose instruction expired without finishing.

Exposed because the scheduler is not implemented yet and an administrator
needs a way to clear a host whose agent never came back — stated rather
than implied, so nobody mistakes this endpoint for the mechanism. When the
reconciliation loop lands this becomes a manual nudge rather than the only
path.

get.description:
Every host's update situation, for the table.

Not paginated, deliberately: the fleet is bounded at 500 connections by
``MAX_CONNECTIONS`` and this is one row per host with no joins per row.
Paginating it would add a cursor to a page that wants to be sorted and
filtered in the browser.

schema.title: Response Host Update Statuses Api V1 Updates Hosts Get

post.description:
Stop an update that has not got too far.

Refused from ``installing`` onwards: the binary is being replaced on a
machine the controller cannot reach into, so cancelling would be a promise
it cannot keep. The agent's own rollback is what recovers from there, and
the refusal says so.

get.description:
How an update got where it did, oldest first.

"It reached staged and then failed" and "it never got past queued" are
different problems with the same final state, and this is where that
difference lives.

schema.title: Response Update Events Api V1 Updates Jobs  Job Id  Events Get

get.description:
What the fleet is running, and what is available.

Available to every authenticated role: a viewer who cannot see that the
fleet is two versions behind cannot do their job.
List rollouts with their progress. Any authenticated role may read.

schema.title: Response List Rollouts Api V1 Updates Rollouts Get

post.description:
Create a rollout. Administrator only, and audited.

**Nothing starts here.** The rollout is `pending` and a background pass
starts its canary — within the maintenance window, if one was given.

get.summary: One rollout and every member's state

post.description:
Cancel. Members that have not started never will.

In-flight jobs are **not** cancelled: the job has its own cancel, per
host, and reaching for a fleet-level button to abandon an install that is
replacing a binary is a bigger hammer than anybody wants.

Pause. In-flight installs finish; nothing new starts.

Deliberately not a cancellation of what is running: an install halfway
through replacing a binary is the worst moment to abandon, and the
agent's own rollback is what handles a bad one.

Resume a paused rollout.

`override_failures` is the administrator saying "I have looked at the
canary that failed and I want the rest anyway". It is recorded on the
rollout rather than implied by the resume, because "resumed after a
failure" and "resumed after an administrator paused it" are different
facts and the second must not be able to look like the first.

get.description:
Return a page of accounts.

``limit`` is bounded by the query validation *and* clamped again in the
service. Two layers on purpose: this is the bound that stops an
authenticated caller asking the server to materialise the whole table, and
a bound enforced in only one place is one a future caller can route
around.

schema.title: Is Active

post.description:
Create an account and return it.

The response carries **no password material** — not the plaintext that was
submitted, not the hash, not a token. An administrator who needs to give
the password to its owner already has it: they chose it.

422.description: The username, display name or password is invalid.

get.description:
Return one account.

``user_id`` is typed as a UUID, so a malformed id is a 422 from the
framework and never reaches a query.

patch.description:
Apply an administrative change.

Partial by design: a request naming only ``role`` leaves the display name
and status alone. An empty body is accepted and changes nothing, which is
the honest answer — refusing it would mean the client had to decide
whether its own diff was empty, and a no-op is not an error.

409.description: The change would leave no active administrator.

patch.summary: Change a user's display name, role or status

post.description:
End an account's access.

Takes effect immediately: ``is_active`` is re-checked on every request, so
the account's next call fails whether or not its session has expired. Its
live sessions are also revoked, so the session counts an administrator
sees afterwards are accurate.

Idempotent — deactivating an already-inactive account succeeds and records
nothing.

409.description: This is the only active administrator.

post.description:
Restore an account's access.

Does **not** restore the sessions deactivation revoked, and must not: a
revoked token is revoked. The account signs in again, which is also the
only way the server learns the password is still known to its owner.

End every live session for an account, without changing its status.

Distinct from deactivation: the account may sign in again straight away.
This is the "I think that session was taken over" action, not the "this
person has left" action.

Returns the count, so the interface can report what happened rather than
asserting success. A revocation that reports success without having
revoked anything is the one thing this must not do, which is why an
unknown id is a 404 rather than a cheerful zero.
post.summary: Revoke all of a user's sessions

get.description:
Return 200 whenever the process is able to serve requests.

Public and intentionally uninformative. The version is available to an
authenticated caller at ``GET /api/v1/info``.

Verify every dependency required to serve traffic.

Public, so the response is an aggregate. Which dependency failed and why
goes to the log, not to an anonymous caller.
